name: Browsing policy definitions
purpose: Look through the loaded policy templates: categories, products, support rules, template files and policies, and open the details of each.

layers.name: Dialog windows and their reactions
layers.summary: What a person sees and enters in the program's windows, and the routines that answer each click, selection and window event before handing the choices to the policy code.
layers.detail: What a person sees and enters in the program's windows, and the routines that answer each click, selection and window event before handing the choices to the policy code.

layers.name: Policy definitions and files
layers.summary: Reads the administrative template and comment files, joins them into policies, categories and products, and holds the data shapes those steps use.

layers.name: Program setup and settings
layers.summary: Settings that tell Windows how to run the program and the helper that keeps the person's choices between runs.

rules.headline: Top-level products list shows every loaded product ordered…
rules.detail: The top-level products list shows every loaded product ordered by name, each with its number of children.

rules.headline: Folder box and its Browse button are usable…
rules.detail: The folder box and its Browse button are usable only when the 'This folder' choice is selected.

rules.headline: Semantic Policy fragment shows one section per area…
rules.summary: The Semantic Policy fragment shows one section per area the policy applies to: the machine section reads the computer source and its comments
rules.detail: The Semantic Policy fragment shows one section per area the policy applies to: the machine section reads the computer source and its comments, the user section reads the user source and its comments; an area the policy does not cover is left out.

rules.headline: Policy inspector shows a "Registry value" line…
rules.detail: The policy inspector shows a "Registry value" line for the policy only when the policy names a registry value.

rules.headline: Policy inspector shows a "Client extension" line…
rules.detail: The policy inspector shows a "Client extension" line for the policy only when the policy names a client extension.

rules.headline: Support definitions list shows only definitions whose name…
rules.summary: The support definitions list shows only definitions whose name contains the typed filter text, ignoring upper or lower case; an empty filter shows all.
rules.detail: The support definitions list shows only definitions whose name contains the typed filter text, ignoring upper or lower case; an empty filter shows all. Entries are ordered by name with leading spaces ignored and shown without them.

rules.headline: Policy details window names the section a policy…
rules.detail: The policy details window names the section a policy applies to: "User or computer" when it applies to both, "Computer" when machine-only, "User" when user-only.

rules.headline: Support details window states how a support definition…
rules.summary: The support details window states how a support definition matches products: "Match all the referenced products", "Match any of the referenced products"
rules.detail: The support details window states how a support definition matches products: "Match all the referenced products", "Match any of the referenced products", or "Do not match products" when it has no matching logic.

rules.headline: When the ADMX folder dialog opens
rules.summary: When the ADMX folder dialog opens, 'This folder' is chosen first
rules.detail: When the ADMX folder dialog opens, 'This folder' is chosen first, and the 'The domain's SYSVOL' choice is available only if the computer is joined to a domain and the folder \\domain\SYSVOL\domain\Policies\PolicyDefinitions exists.

rules.headline: Product details window labels a product "Major revision"
rules.detail: The product details window labels a product "Major revision", "Minor revision" or "Top-level product" from its type.

rules.headline: Detail window of a category shows its parent's…
rules.summary: The detail window of a category shows its parent's name and enables the parent button when the parent exists; when the parent is named
rules.detail: The detail window of a category shows its parent's name and enables the parent button when the parent exists; when the parent is named but missing it shows "<orphaned from <parent>>" and the button is disabled; a top-level category shows nothing.

rules.headline: Within each section of the fragment
rules.summary: Within each section of the fragment, the policy comment is included only when one is stored for that policy
rules.detail: Within each section of the fragment, the policy comment is included only when one is stored for that policy, and the option values are included only when the policy is Enabled.

rules.headline: Detail window of a template file lists only…
rules.summary: The detail window of a template file lists only the policies, categories (including sub-categories), products (including versions) and support rules that were defined in
rules.detail: The detail window of a template file lists only the policies, categories (including sub-categories), products (including versions) and support rules that were defined in that file.

rules.headline: Double-clicking the loaded ADMX files list opens…
rules.detail: Double-clicking the loaded ADMX files list opens the file details for the selected row without checking that a row is selected; pressing Enter does check.

rules.headline: When a policy names a support definition
rules.summary: When a policy names a support definition that exists, its name is shown and the support-details button is enabled.
rules.detail: When a policy names a support definition that exists, its name is shown and the support-details button is enabled. When it does not exist, the button is disabled and the text reads "<missing: " followed by the code the policy names; with no code the text is blank.

rules.headline: Each entry of a support definition is listed…
rules.summary: Each entry of a support definition is listed by the name of the nested support definition when it is one
rules.detail: Each entry of a support definition is listed by the name of the nested support definition when it is one, otherwise by the name of the product, otherwise as "<missing: " followed by the product code the entry names. Minimum and maximum versions are listed only for product entries that name a version range; a missing bound is shown blank.

rules.headline: Double-clicking the support definitions list opens the definition…
rules.detail: Double-clicking the support definitions list opens the definition details for the selected row without checking that a row is selected; pressing Enter does check.

rules.headline: Product details window shows a version number…
rules.detail: The product details window shows a version number for major and minor revisions only; for a top-level product the version is blank.

rules.headline: Product with a parent shows the parent name…
rules.summary: A product with a parent shows the parent name and enables the parent button
rules.detail: A product with a parent shows the parent name and enables the parent button; a product with no parent shows a blank parent and the button is disabled.

rules.headline: Major versions list shows the children…
rules.summary: The major versions list shows the children of the selected top-level product ordered by version, with the heading naming that product
rules.detail: The major versions list shows the children of the selected top-level product ordered by version, with the heading naming that product; with no product selected it is empty and prompts the person to select one.

rules.headline: When a policy sits in a category
rules.summary: When a policy sits in a category that exists, the category name is shown and the category-details button is enabled.
rules.detail: When a policy sits in a category that exists, the category name is shown and the category-details button is enabled. A policy whose named category is unknown shows "<orphaned from " followed by that category code, and one with no category code shows "<uncategorized>"; the button is then disabled.

rules.headline: When OK is pressed in the ADMX folder…
rules.summary: When OK is pressed in the ADMX folder dialog, the folder is the system's Windows PolicyDefinitions folder, the domain SYSVOL folder, or the typed folder
rules.detail: When OK is pressed in the ADMX folder dialog, the folder is the system's Windows PolicyDefinitions folder, the domain SYSVOL folder, or the typed folder, as chosen. A folder that does not exist is refused with "The folder you specified does not exist." and the dialog stays open.

rules.headline: Product details window lists every child revision…
rules.detail: The product details window lists every child revision of a product with its version and name; a product with no children shows an empty list.

rules.headline: Option to clear the workspace
rules.summary: The option to clear the workspace before adding the folder is ticked by default, and its choice is passed on only when a folder
rules.detail: The option to clear the workspace before adding the folder is ticked by default, and its choice is passed on only when a folder that exists was accepted.

rules.headline: Fragment text starts with the heading "Policy Plus…
rules.summary: The fragment text starts with the heading "Policy Plus Semantic Policy" and a blank line only when "Include SPOL header" is ticked
rules.detail: The fragment text starts with the heading "Policy Plus Semantic Policy" and a blank line only when "Include SPOL header" is ticked; otherwise only the fragment is shown.

rules.headline: Clearing the search forgets the results
rules.detail: Clearing the search forgets the results, so reopening them reports that no search has been run.

rules.headline: Double-clicking a child revision in the product details…
rules.detail: Double-clicking a child revision in the product details window shows that child in the same window; with nothing selected, nothing happens.

rules.headline: Minor versions list shows the children…
rules.summary: The minor versions list shows the children of the selected major version ordered by version, with the heading naming it
rules.detail: The minor versions list shows the children of the selected major version ordered by version, with the heading naming it; with no major version selected it is empty and prompts the person to select one.

rules.headline: Double-clicking an entry in the support details window…
rules.summary: Double-clicking an entry in the support details window opens the product details window for a product entry
rules.detail: Double-clicking an entry in the support details window opens the product details window for a product entry, and shows a nested support definition in the same window. An entry whose product is missing, or with nothing selected, does nothing.

rules.headline: Pressing Escape closes the ADMX folder dialog…
rules.detail: Pressing Escape closes the ADMX folder dialog as cancelled, with no folder chosen.

rules.headline: Opening product details by double-click or Enter does…
rules.detail: Opening product details by double-click or Enter does nothing when no product is selected in that list.

rules.headline: In the inspector
rules.summary: In the inspector, a group of affected registry settings with no on or off setting reads "Left implicit" when the policy names a registry value
rules.detail: In the inspector, a group of affected registry settings with no on or off setting reads "Left implicit" when the policy names a registry value, and "Left to elements" when it names none. Inside a Yes/No element it always reads "Left implicit".

rules.headline: Policy inspector lists presentation details for the policy…
rules.summary: The policy inspector lists presentation details for the policy whenever it has both a presentation and elements, whatever the elements hold.
rules.detail: The policy inspector lists presentation details for the policy whenever it has both a presentation and elements, whatever the elements hold. Each presentation item with an ID is matched to the policy element with the same ID; items without an ID show no element details. When no element has that ID, the inspector stops with an unhandled error.

rules.headline: Category appears in the tree only when it…
rules.summary: A category appears in the tree only when it passes the visibility rule
rules.detail: A category appears in the tree only when it passes the visibility rule; each shown category gets an icon by its kind and carries its visible subcategories below it, and the tree is sorted.

rules.headline: After the category tree is rebuilt…
rules.summary: After the category tree is rebuilt from the loaded definitions, no category
rules.detail: After the category tree is rebuilt from the loaded definitions, no category, policy or highlighted item is selected and the information pane shows the empty state.

rules.headline: When the list is rebuilt
rules.summary: When the list is rebuilt, the policy already selected is selected again and revealed only if it is still listed, that is
rules.detail: When the list is rebuilt, the policy already selected is selected again and revealed only if it is still listed, that is, it sits in the category shown and passes the visibility rule; otherwise nothing is selected. Then, if the policy is in the same category and the list still has that many rows, the earlier top row is put back, so the policy is not guaranteed to stay in view.

rules.headline: Right pane lists the chosen category in this…
rules.summary: The right pane lists the chosen category in this order: an "Up: <parent name>" row marked "Parent" when the category has a parent
rules.detail: The right pane lists the chosen category in this order: an "Up: <parent name>" row marked "Parent" when the category has a parent, then visible subcategories by name, then visible policies by name. Each policy row shows its state and its comment text.

rules.headline: Category tree selection follows the category shown…
rules.detail: The category tree selection follows the category shown in the right pane.

rules.headline: For a list element the inspector states how…
rules.summary: For a list element the inspector states how value names are formed: "User provides value names" when the person names them
rules.detail: For a list element the inspector states how value names are formed: "User provides value names" when the person names them, a prefix when the element has one, otherwise "No prefix (values named for their data)".

rules.headline: When nothing is selected
rules.detail: When nothing is selected, the title and support lines are hidden and the pane reads "Select an item to see its description.".

rules.headline: For a selected policy the information pane shows…
rules.summary: For a selected policy the information pane shows its title, "(no requirements information)" when it has no support rule or "Requirements:" plus the support name
rules.detail: For a selected policy the information pane shows its title, "(no requirements information)" when it has no support rule or "Requirements:" plus the support name, and its explanation. A notice that the policy is a preference appears only for preferences.

rules.headline: Choice display names in the inspector are resolved…
rules.detail: Choice display names in the inspector are resolved through the definitions file that defines the policy, and choices are numbered from zero in file order.

rules.headline: For a selected or highlighted category the pane…
rules.summary: " ("The selected category" when highlighted but not opened) and its explanation. The counts include every policy and subcategory, hidden or not.
rules.detail: For a selected or highlighted category the pane shows its title, "This category contains N policies and M subcategories." ("The selected category" when highlighted but not opened) and its explanation. The counts include every policy and subcategory, hidden or not.

rules.headline: Category is orphaned when it has no parent…
rules.detail: A category is orphaned when it has no parent among the loaded definitions although its definition names one.

rules.headline: Category is empty when it holds no subcategories…
rules.detail: A category is empty when it holds no subcategories and no policies at all, counting hidden ones.

rules.headline: Category's icon is chosen in this order: orphaned
rules.detail: A category's icon is chosen in this order: orphaned, then empty, then normal.

rules.headline: Policy's icon is chosen in this order: preference
rules.detail: A policy's icon is chosen in this order: preference, then plain when it has no configurable elements, then "extra configuration" when it has some.

rules.headline: Inspector copies the selected line to the clipboard…
rules.detail: The inspector copies the selected line to the clipboard only on Ctrl+C with a line selected.

rules.headline: Category is visible when empty categories are switched…
rules.summary: A category is visible when empty categories are switched on.
rules.detail: A category is visible when empty categories are switched on. Otherwise it is visible only if it has at least one visible policy or one visible subcategory.

rules.headline: Policy is visible only if it applies…
rules.summary: A policy is visible only if it applies to a chosen area (user, computer or both).
rules.detail: A policy is visible only if it applies to a chosen area (user, computer or both). With "Only Filtered Policies" on, it must also pass the filter for a chosen area it applies to; passing for either one is enough.

rules.headline: When a view setting changes
rules.summary: When a view setting changes, the program moves up to the nearest visible category
rules.detail: When a view setting changes, the program moves up to the nearest visible category, drops the selected policy if the move happened or the policy is now hidden, then rebuilds the tree and list. A policy kept after the move appears in the information pane only: rebuilding the list reselects the category in the tree, which clears the selection, so its row is not highlighted.

rules.headline: With both areas shown, a policy
rules.summary: With both areas shown, a policy that applies to both areas shows its common state followed by "(2)" when both match
rules.detail: With both areas shown, a policy that applies to both areas shows its common state followed by "(2)" when both match, the computer state followed by "(C)" when only the user is Not Configured, the user state followed by "(U)" when only the computer is Not Configured, and "Mixed" otherwise.

rules.headline: With both areas shown, a policy
rules.summary: With both areas shown, a policy that applies to one area shows that area's state followed by "(C)" for computer or "(U)" for user.
rules.detail: With both areas shown, a policy that applies to one area shows that area's state followed by "(C)" for computer or "(U)" for user. With a single area shown, only that area's state is shown, without a suffix.

rules.headline: Policy's state in one area reads "Enabled", "Disabled"
rules.summary: A policy's state in one area reads "Enabled", "Disabled", "Not Configured" or "Unknown"
rules.detail: A policy's state in one area reads "Enabled", "Disabled", "Not Configured" or "Unknown"; the computer source is read for the computer area and the user source for any other.

rules.headline: With both areas shown
rules.summary: With both areas shown, the comment column is empty when neither area has a comment, shows "(multiple)" when both have one
rules.detail: With both areas shown, the comment column is empty when neither area has a comment, shows "(multiple)" when both have one, and otherwise shows the single comment.

rules.headline: Policy's comment in one area is empty when
rules.summary: A policy's comment in one area is empty when that source has no comment file or holds no comment for the policy
rules.detail: A policy's comment in one area is empty when that source has no comment file or holds no comment for the policy, and otherwise the saved text.

rules.headline: Policy is a preference, not a managed policy
rules.detail: A policy is a preference, not a managed policy, when it names a registry key outside the three policy locations: software\policies, software\microsoft\windows\currentversion\policies and system\currentcontrolset\policies.

rules.headline: After the edit dialog is accepted
rules.summary: After the edit dialog is accepted, which changes the open policy source in memory only
rules.detail: After the edit dialog is accepted, which changes the open policy source in memory only, the list is refreshed in place if the current category is still visible; otherwise the program moves up to the nearest visible category. Nothing is written to disk until Save Policies.

rules.headline: Closing the workspace or replacing it…
rules.detail: Closing the workspace or replacing it with a new one discards all loaded definitions and the previous search results.

rules.headline: Filter on managed policies hides preferences when managed…
rules.detail: A filter on managed policies hides preferences when managed policies are wanted, and hides managed policies when preferences are wanted.

rules.headline: Policy passes the filter only when it passes…
rules.detail: A policy passes the filter only when it passes every active part of it.

rules.headline: Filter on state keeps only policies whose state…
rules.detail: A filter on state keeps only policies whose state in the checked area is Configured (Enabled or Disabled), Not Configured, Disabled or Enabled, as chosen.

rules.headline: Filter on comments keeps only policies
rules.detail: A filter on comments keeps only policies that have a non-empty comment in the checked area, or only those that have none, as chosen.

rules.headline: Filter on products keeps only policies supported…
rules.summary: A filter on products keeps only policies supported by the chosen products
rules.detail: A filter on products keeps only policies supported by the chosen products, honouring the options to match any product and to include policies with blank support.

rules.headline: Policy applies to an area when its definition…
rules.detail: A policy applies to an area when its definition declares that area; a policy declared for both applies to each.

rules.headline: When loading definitions reports no problems nothing…
rules.detail: When loading definitions reports no problems nothing is shown; otherwise the person sees "Errors were encountered while adding administrative templates to the workspace." with each problem, and, only where a choice is wanted, is asked "Continue trying to use this workspace?".

rules.headline: Language for definition text is the saved language…
rules.detail: The language for definition text is the saved language code, or the computer's own language when none is saved.

rules.headline: Selecting a category in the tree makes it…
rules.detail: Selecting a category in the tree makes it the current category and clears any selected policy.

rules.headline: Highlighting a policy makes it the selected policy…
rules.detail: Highlighting a policy makes it the selected policy and clears any highlighted category; highlighting a category does the reverse; highlighting nothing clears both.

rules.headline: When a definitions folder is opened
rules.summary: When a definitions folder is opened, the workspace is emptied first only if "clear workspace" is chosen.
rules.detail: When a definitions folder is opened, the workspace is emptied first only if "clear workspace" is chosen. Otherwise the folder's definitions are added to the current workspace. Problems found are reported but do not stop the load.

rules.headline: Definitions folder is remembered as the definitions folder…
rules.summary: A definitions folder is remembered as the definitions folder for the next start only when "clear workspace" was chosen and the load did not fail
rules.detail: A definitions folder is remembered as the definitions folder for the next start only when "clear workspace" was chosen and the load did not fail; when the workspace is added to, the remembered folder is unchanged.

rules.headline: When opening a definitions folder fails
rules.summary: " with the reason. The workspace may already be emptied or partly filled, the remembered folder is unchanged, and the view is rebuilt anyway.
rules.detail: When opening a definitions folder fails, the person is told "The folder could not be fully added to the workspace." with the reason. The workspace may already be emptied or partly filled, the remembered folder is unchanged, and the view is rebuilt anyway.

rules.headline: Single ADMX file picked from the file dialog…
rules.summary: " with the reason.
rules.detail: A single ADMX file picked from the file dialog (ADMX files only) is added to the current workspace without emptying it and is not remembered as the definitions folder; a failure shows "The ADMX file could not be added to the workspace." with the reason.

rules.headline: Closing the workspace from the menu empties it…
rules.detail: Closing the workspace from the menu empties it at once with no confirmation and rebuilds the view.

rules.headline: "Empty Categories" menu switches empty categories…
rules.detail: The "Empty Categories" menu switches empty categories on or off and the view moves to the nearest visible category.

rules.headline: Area choice "User" shows user policies
rules.detail: The area choice "User" shows user policies, "Computer" shows computer policies and any other choice shows both.

rules.headline: Opening an item in the policy list does…
rules.summary: Opening an item in the policy list does nothing with no selection, opens a category as the current one
rules.detail: Opening an item in the policy list does nothing with no selection, opens a category as the current one, or opens a policy's editor for the area currently shown; Enter does the same.

rules.headline: Policy deduplication merges otherwise identical user and computer…
rules.detail: Policy deduplication merges otherwise identical user and computer policy pairs into single policies that apply to both and tells the person "Deduplicated N policies.".

rules.headline: When the right-click menu is opened…
rules.summary: When the right-click menu is opened from the category tree, it is shown for the selected category
rules.detail: When the right-click menu is opened from the category tree, it is shown for the selected category, and a tree with no selected category is not handled (the program fails with an error). When opened from anywhere else with a row selected in the policy list, it is shown for that row. When opened from anywhere else with no row selected, it is not shown.

rules.headline: Right-click menu shows only the actions
rules.summary: The right-click menu shows only the actions that fit what was clicked: policy-only actions are hidden for a category
rules.detail: The right-click menu shows only the actions that fit what was clicked: policy-only actions are hidden for a category, and category-only actions are hidden for a policy.

rules.headline: When a category in the tree is right-clicked
rules.summary: When a category in the tree is right-clicked, it becomes the selected category, because a right-click alone does not select it
rules.detail: When a category in the tree is right-clicked, it becomes the selected category, because a right-click alone does not select it; a left-click is left as is.

rules.headline: Text of a policy description is tidied…
rules.summary: The text of a policy description is tidied for display
rules.detail: The text of a policy description is tidied for display: leading and trailing spaces are removed from every line and blank space at the end of the text is dropped.

rules.headline: An XML attribute that is absent gives nothing
rules.detail: An XML attribute that is absent gives nothing.

rules.headline: XML attribute that is absent
rules.detail: An XML attribute that is absent, or whose text is not valid for the type of the stated default, gives that default.

rules.headline: Policy's lists of on-values and off-values count…
rules.summary: A policy's lists of on-values and off-values count as enabled or disabled evidence for each value in them that is present
rules.detail: A policy's lists of on-values and off-values count as enabled or disabled evidence for each value in them that is present, using the list's own key when it names one.

rules.headline: When a language file has no policy resources…
rules.summary: When a language file has no policy resources section, or its revision is missing or not a number
rules.detail: When a language file has no policy resources section, or its revision is missing or not a number, the file is refused as invalid and its template file is not loaded.

rules.headline: Template file is refused as invalid when any…
rules.summary: A template file is refused as invalid when any of these is missing or unreadable: the policy definitions section; a namespace entry's prefix or namespace
rules.detail: A template file is refused as invalid when any of these is missing or unreadable: the policy definitions section; a namespace entry's prefix or namespace; a superseded-ADM file name; a minimum revision (missing or not a number); a support rule's name or display name; a support reference or range without its reference, or a version bound that is not a whole number; a product's name, display name or version index; a category's name or display name; a category's parent entry or its reference when the category has content; a policy's name, display name, key or class; a policy's category or supported-on reference; a number value's value; a list item's value name; a choice item's display name; or an option's id.

rules.headline: Only files directly in the chosen folder whose…
rules.summary: admx (in any letter case) are loaded as templates; subfolders and other files are ignored.
rules.detail: Only files directly in the chosen folder whose names end in .admx (in any letter case) are loaded as templates; subfolders and other files are ignored.

rules.headline: Policy with a registry value of its own…
rules.summary: A policy with a registry value of its own counts as enabled evidence when that value holds its 'on' value
rules.detail: A policy with a registry value of its own counts as enabled evidence when that value holds its 'on' value, which is the number 1 when the template gives none, and as disabled evidence when it holds its 'off' value or is marked for deletion when the template gives none.

rules.headline: When a template file is refused…
rules.summary: When a template file is refused with a reported failure (unparsable, invalid, namespace already owned, or no usable language file)
rules.detail: When a template file is refused with a reported failure (unparsable, invalid, namespace already owned, or no usable language file), it is skipped and the failure is listed; the other files in the folder still load and the structures are built from those that loaded.

rules.headline: Namespace of a template is the one listed…
rules.summary: The namespace of a template is the one listed as its target; each prefix a template declares must be unique
rules.detail: The namespace of a template is the one listed as its target; each prefix a template declares must be unique, and a repeated prefix refuses the file as invalid.

rules.headline: Language file's text table is read only…
rules.summary: A language file's text table is read only from its first text table, and each text is kept under its id
rules.detail: A language file's text table is read only from its first text table, and each text is kept under its id; when the same text id appears twice, the file is refused as invalid and its template file is not loaded.

rules.headline: Template's superseded-ADM file name and minimum language revision…
rules.summary: A template's superseded-ADM file name and minimum language revision are read when present; a superseded entry without a file name, or a minimum revision
rules.detail: A template's superseded-ADM file name and minimum language revision are read when present; a superseded entry without a file name, or a minimum revision that is missing or not a number, refuses the template as invalid.

rules.headline: Loading a single template file adds
rules.summary: Loading a single template file adds that file alone to the policies already loaded, builds the structures
rules.detail: Loading a single template file adds that file alone to the policies already loaded, builds the structures, and reports one failure when the file is refused.

rules.headline: When a template file cannot be parsed…
rules.summary: "; any other read problem is refused with "The ADMX is invalid: <detail>".
rules.detail: When a template file cannot be parsed as XML, it is refused with the message "Couldn't load <path>: The ADMX XML couldn't be parsed: <detail>."; any other read problem is refused with "The ADMX is invalid: <detail>".

rules.headline: Language file's screen layouts are read only…
rules.summary: A language file's screen layouts are read only from its first presentation table; when the same layout id appears twice
rules.detail: A language file's screen layouts are read only from its first presentation table; when the same layout id appears twice, the file is refused as invalid and its template file is not loaded.

rules.headline: For a policy's list elements
rules.summary: For a policy's list elements, a marked-for-deletion list counts as one deleted element, and a list
rules.detail: For a policy's list elements, a marked-for-deletion list counts as one deleted element, and a list that holds any values counts as a present element and cancels that deletion.

rules.headline: Support rule is 'any of' when its first…
rules.summary: A support rule is 'any of' when its first logic element is "or", 'all of' when it is "and", and blank otherwise; only
rules.detail: A support rule is 'any of' when its first logic element is "or", 'all of' when it is "and", and blank otherwise; only that first logic element is read, each reference or range in it becomes an entry, and a range may carry a minimum and maximum version.

rules.headline: When a template file's namespace is already held…
rules.summary: When a template file's namespace is already held by a template file loaded earlier
rules.detail: When a template file's namespace is already held by a template file loaded earlier, it is refused with "The <namespace> namespace is already owned by a different ADMX file", so the same file cannot be added twice.

rules.headline: When a template declares no target namespace
rules.summary: When a template declares no target namespace, loading the folder stops at once with an error: the files after it are not read
rules.detail: When a template declares no target namespace, loading the folder stops at once with an error: the files after it are not read, nothing is built, and the person sees the error text (a start-up load also discards the workspace).

rules.headline: Language file for a template is taken…
rules.summary: The language file for a template is taken from the subfolder named exactly by the language code if it holds this template's file
rules.detail: The language file for a template is taken from the subfolder named exactly by the language code if it holds this template's file; else from the first subfolder whose name starts with the same language part (before the dash, compared with capital letters mattering) that holds this template's file; else from the en-US subfolder if it holds it. A folder lacking the file is skipped.

rules.headline: For a checkbox element
rules.summary: For a checkbox element: a value marked for deletion counts as one deleted element.
rules.detail: For a checkbox element: a value marked for deletion counts as one deleted element. Otherwise, each present off value (or off-list value) counts a tenth of a deleted element, and each present on value (or on-list value) counts one present element. A checkbox whose template declares no on value or on list adds no present evidence, even if it holds 1.

rules.headline: Number box takes default value 1
rules.summary: A number box takes default value 1, shows its up-down spinner and steps by 1 unless the language file says otherwise
rules.detail: A number box takes default value 1, shows its up-down spinner and steps by 1 unless the language file says otherwise; an unreadable attribute value falls back to the same defaults.

rules.headline: When no language file is found in any…
rules.summary: When no language file is found in any of those places
rules.detail: When no language file is found in any of those places, the template file is refused with "The corresponding ADML is missing" and none of its content is loaded.

rules.headline: For any other element (number, text, choice
rules.summary: For any other element (number, text, choice, multi-line text), a value marked for deletion counts as a deleted element and a value
rules.detail: For any other element (number, text, choice, multi-line text), a value marked for deletion counts as a deleted element and a value that is present counts as a present element.

rules.headline: When the chosen language file cannot be parsed…
rules.summary: When the chosen language file cannot be parsed as XML, the template is refused with "The ADML XML couldn't be parsed: <detail>"
rules.detail: When the chosen language file cannot be parsed as XML, the template is refused with "The ADML XML couldn't be parsed: <detail>"; any other read problem gives "The ADML is invalid: <detail>".

rules.headline: If any element is present
rules.summary: If any element is present, the elements add their count to the enabled evidence
rules.detail: If any element is present, the elements add their count to the enabled evidence; only when none is present do deleted elements add to the disabled evidence.

rules.headline: When both a template file and its language…
rules.summary: When both a template file and its language file load, the template's categories, products
rules.detail: When both a template file and its language file load, the template's categories, products, support rules and policies are staged for the next build and the pair is recorded as loaded under the template's namespace.

rules.headline: Check box starts unticked
rules.detail: A check box starts unticked unless the language file marks it ticked.

rules.headline: Products form three levels: a product
rules.summary: Products form three levels: a product, its major versions and their minor versions; deeper levels are not read
rules.detail: Products form three levels: a product, its major versions and their minor versions; deeper levels are not read, and each version must carry a version index or the file is refused as invalid.

rules.headline: Policy is Enabled when enabled evidence exceeds disabled…
rules.summary: A policy is Enabled when enabled evidence exceeds disabled evidence, Disabled when disabled exceeds enabled, Not configured when there is no evidence either way
rules.detail: A policy is Enabled when enabled evidence exceeds disabled evidence, Disabled when disabled exceeds enabled, Not configured when there is no evidence either way, and Unclear when both are equal and above zero.

rules.headline: Entries of a combo box or drop-down list…
rules.detail: Entries of a combo box or drop-down list are sorted unless the language file says not to sort them.

rules.headline: Value counts as present when
rules.summary: A value counts as present when: for a deletion marker, it is marked for deletion; for a number
rules.detail: A value counts as present when: for a deletion marker, it is marked for deletion; for a number, it exists as a whole number and equals the expected number; for text, it exists as text and equals the expected text. A value of the wrong kind is not present.

rules.headline: Drop-down list has a preselected item only…
rules.detail: A drop-down list has a preselected item only when the language file names one; otherwise none is preselected.

rules.headline: Category's explanation is optional
rules.summary: A category's explanation is optional.
rules.detail: A category's explanation is optional. A category with any content inside it (even a comment) must contain a parent entry with a reference; otherwise the template is refused as invalid.

rules.headline: Only labels, number boxes, text boxes, check boxes
rules.summary: Only labels, number boxes, text boxes, check boxes, combo boxes, drop-down lists, list boxes and multi-line text boxes are kept in a screen layout
rules.detail: Only labels, number boxes, text boxes, check boxes, combo boxes, drop-down lists, list boxes and multi-line text boxes are kept in a screen layout; any other control in the language file is dropped without notice.

rules.headline: List of values counts as present only…
rules.detail: A list of values counts as present only when every value in it is present.

rules.headline: Control keeps the reference id the language file…
rules.summary: A control keeps the reference id the language file gives it, which ties it to the matching setting option in the template file
rules.detail: A control keeps the reference id the language file gives it, which ties it to the matching setting option in the template file; a control without one has no id.

rules.headline: Value in a policy file counts as present…
rules.detail: A value in a policy file counts as present only if it is stored and not marked for deletion.

rules.headline: Two policies are merged into one for both…
rules.summary: Two policies are merged into one for both sections when they are alone in the same category under the same name
rules.detail: Two policies are merged into one for both sections when they are alone in the same category under the same name, one is for users and the other for computers, and both have the same explanation text and the same registry key; the first is removed and the second becomes a both-sections policy.

rules.headline: Reading a value from a policy file gives…
rules.detail: Reading a value from a policy file gives nothing when the value is absent or marked for deletion.

rules.headline: Registry value in a template is a delete…
rules.summary: A registry value in a template is a delete marker, a number or a text, decided by the first of those it contains
rules.detail: A registry value in a template is a delete marker, a number or a text, decided by the first of those it contains; a value with none of them is treated as a delete marker.

rules.headline: Value in a policy file counts as marked…
rules.summary: A value in a policy file counts as marked for deletion when a deletion marker names it, when the key has a clear-all marker
rules.detail: A value in a policy file counts as marked for deletion when a deletion marker names it, when the key has a clear-all marker, or when a delete-values list for the key names it, regardless of case. Entries are examined in sorted order, and a value whose name sorts after the marker is stored as present and cancels the deletion, whenever it was written and whichever marker kind came before.

rules.headline: Policy gets a settings screen layout only…
rules.summary: <id>)", and the language file holds a layout with that id; in every other case the policy has none.
rules.detail: A policy gets a settings screen layout only when the template names one, the name is written as "$(presentation.<id>)", and the language file holds a layout with that id; in every other case the policy has none.

rules.headline: Category whose parent is named is attached under
rules.summary: A category whose parent is named is attached under that parent, found among items of this load or of files loaded earlier
rules.detail: A category whose parent is named is attached under that parent, found among items of this load or of files loaded earlier; when the parent is not found, the category has no parent but is still listed among the top-level categories.

rules.headline: Semantic policy text line shows 'C'…
rules.detail: A semantic policy text line shows 'C' for a machine policy and 'U' for a user policy, followed by the identifier.

rules.headline: When a policy is written as semantic policy…
rules.summary: When a policy is written as semantic policy text
rules.detail: When a policy is written as semantic policy text, backslashes in its comment are doubled and each carriage return plus line feed pair is written as '\n'. A lone line feed or lone carriage return is written as it is, which splits the comment over two script lines and corrupts it when read back.

rules.headline: Policy's switched-on and switched-off effects are read…
rules.summary: A policy's switched-on and switched-off effects are read from its enabled and disabled values and lists
rules.detail: A policy's switched-on and switched-off effects are read from its enabled and disabled values and lists; a list entry names a value and optionally its own key, falling back to the list's default key.

rules.headline: Child product (major or minor version) is attached…
rules.summary: A child product (major or minor version) is attached under its parent product, which must be defined in the same template file
rules.detail: A child product (major or minor version) is attached under its parent product, which must be defined in the same template file; only products without a parent are listed as top-level products.

rules.headline: Listing the values of a key…
rules.detail: Listing the values of a key in a policy file leaves out the marker entries unless the caller asks for them.

rules.headline: Saved value of a number or text element…
rules.summary: The saved value of a number or text element is read as stored; the reading assumes the value exists and is of the right kind
rules.detail: The saved value of a number or text element is read as stored; the reading assumes the value exists and is of the right kind, and is not checked first. A checkbox is read by its own rule.

rules.headline: Support rule entry is linked to the product…
rules.summary: A support rule entry is linked to the product its reference names; when no such product exists it is linked to the support rule of
rules.detail: A support rule entry is linked to the product its reference names; when no such product exists it is linked to the support rule of that name; when neither exists it stays unlinked.

rules.headline: When a policy is written as semantic policy…
rules.detail: When a policy is written as semantic policy text, its settings are listed only if the policy is Enabled.

rules.headline: List element whose entries have names the person…
rules.detail: A list element whose entries have names the person provides is read as every stored name with its value, under the element's key.

rules.headline: In semantic policy text
rules.summary: In semantic policy text, a whole number is written with a leading #, an unsigned number as digits
rules.detail: In semantic policy text, a whole number is written with a leading #, an unsigned number as digits, and a yes/no value as True or False. Text is written between single quotes with no escaping, so text holding a quote or line break cannot be read back. An empty list is written as 'None'. A list of text is written in brackets, one double-quoted item per line with quotes doubled. A table is written in brackets as double-quoted name: value lines.

rules.headline: Policy is listed under the category its reference…
rules.summary: A policy is listed under the category its reference names, found in this load or earlier ones; when
rules.detail: A policy is listed under the category its reference names, found in this load or earlier ones; when that category is not found the policy is kept in the policy list but belongs to no category.

rules.headline: List element whose entry names do not matter…
rules.summary: A list element whose entry names do not matter is read as a list of values: when the list has a prefix
rules.detail: A list element whose entry names do not matter is read as a list of values: when the list has a prefix, the stored values named prefix1, prefix2, and so on, in order, until the first number that is missing; otherwise every stored value name under the key.

rules.headline: Policy shows the 'supported on' rule its reference…
rules.detail: A policy shows the 'supported on' rule its reference names, found in this load or earlier ones; when none is found it has none.

rules.headline: When the structures are built, all new categories
rules.summary: When the structures are built, all new categories, products, support rules and policies join the final lists and the staged items are cleared
rules.detail: When the structures are built, all new categories, products, support rules and policies join the final lists and the staged items are cleared, so loading further files adds to what is already available.

rules.headline: Choice element is read as the position…
rules.summary: A choice element is read as the position of the first item whose own value is present and, when the item has a value list
rules.detail: A choice element is read as the position of the first item whose own value is present and, when the item has a value list, whose list is wholly present; when no item matches, the position is -1.

rules.headline: Policy applies to computers when its class…
rules.detail: A policy applies to computers when its class is "Machine", to users when "User", and to both for any other class value.

rules.headline: Saved value of a multi-line text element…
rules.detail: The saved value of a multi-line text element is read as stored, without first checking that it exists.

rules.headline: Policy takes its category and its 'supported…
rules.summary: A policy takes its category and its 'supported on' rule from the references in its own content
rules.detail: A policy takes its category and its 'supported on' rule from the references in its own content, and has options only when it contains an options section.

rules.headline: Checkbox is on when its on value…
rules.summary: A checkbox is on when its on value (or all values of its on list) is present, or, with neither defined
rules.detail: A checkbox is on when its on value (or all values of its on list) is present, or, with neither defined, when its value is 1; it is off in every other case, including when its off value is present.

rules.headline: Name or description written as "$(string.<id>)" shows…
rules.summary: A name or description written as "$(string.<id>)" shows the language file's text for that id; an unknown id shows the code itself
rules.detail: A name or description written as "$(string.<id>)" shows the language file's text for that id; an unknown id shows the code itself; any other text is shown as written; an empty value stays empty.

rules.headline: Number option accepts 0 to 4,294,967,295
rules.summary: A number option accepts 0 to 4,294,967,295 unless the template sets other limits, overwrites existing values unless marked soft, and is stored as a number
rules.detail: A number option accepts 0 to 4,294,967,295 unless the template sets other limits, overwrites existing values unless marked soft, and is stored as a number unless marked as text; unreadable attribute values fall back to these defaults.

rules.headline: Yes/no option takes its registry effect for true…
rules.detail: A yes/no option takes its registry effect for true and false from true and false values and lists.

rules.headline: Item's unique name is its template's namespace
rules.detail: An item's unique name is its template's namespace, a colon and its own name, so equal names in different templates stay apart.

rules.headline: Text option allows 255 characters, is optional
rules.summary: A text option allows 255 characters, is optional, is stored as plain text and overwrites existing values unless the template says otherwise
rules.detail: A text option allows 255 characters, is optional, is stored as plain text and overwrites existing values unless the template says otherwise; unreadable attribute values fall back to these defaults.

rules.headline: Reference containing a colon uses the namespace…
rules.summary: A reference containing a colon uses the namespace the template declared for its prefix; with an unknown prefix it is taken as already complete
rules.detail: A reference containing a colon uses the namespace the template declared for its prefix; with an unknown prefix it is taken as already complete; a reference without a colon belongs to the template's own namespace.

rules.headline: REG file cannot be used as a source…
rules.summary: A REG file cannot be used as a source for asking whether a value is present: the request fails with 'not implemented'.
rules.detail: A REG file cannot be used as a source for asking whether a value is present: the request fails with 'not implemented'. Applying a newer policy file over an older one to a REG file fails this way for any dropped value under a policy branch.

rules.headline: List option replaces other entries of its key
rules.summary: A list option replaces other entries of its key unless marked additive, stores plain text unless marked expandable, numbers entries automatically
rules.detail: A list option replaces other entries of its key unless marked additive, stores plain text unless marked expandable, numbers entries automatically unless the template says the person names them, and counts as prefixed only when a value prefix is given.

rules.headline: REG file cannot be used as a source…
rules.summary: A REG file cannot be used as a source for reading a value: the request fails with 'not implemented'.
rules.detail: A REG file cannot be used as a source for reading a value: the request fails with 'not implemented'. Applying a newer policy file over an older one to a REG file fails this way for any dropped value under a policy branch.

rules.headline: REG file cannot be used as a source…
rules.summary: A REG file cannot be used as a source for checking whether a value will be deleted: the request fails with 'not implemented'.
rules.detail: A REG file cannot be used as a source for checking whether a value will be deleted: the request fails with 'not implemented'. Applying a newer policy file over an older one to a REG file fails this way for any dropped value under a policy branch.

rules.headline: REG file cannot be used as a source…
rules.summary: A REG file cannot be used as a source for listing a key's values: the request fails with 'not implemented'.
rules.detail: A REG file cannot be used as a source for listing a key's values: the request fails with 'not implemented'. Applying a newer policy file over an older one to a REG file fails this way for any dropped value under a policy branch.

rules.headline: Choice option is optional unless marked required
rules.summary: A choice option is optional unless marked required.
rules.detail: A choice option is optional unless marked required. Each choice keeps whichever of a single registry value and a list of values it contains, both when both are present; a choice with neither is accepted and changes nothing.

rules.headline: Text read from a policy file stops…
rules.detail: Text read from a policy file stops at its first empty character, and a multiple-string value ends at its first empty string.

rules.headline: Policy option of any kind other than number
rules.detail: A policy option of any kind other than number, yes/no, text, list, choice or multi-line text is dropped without notice.

rules.headline: Option's registry value name is taken…
rules.summary: An option's registry value name is taken from its own value name, except for a list option that has a value prefix attribute
rules.detail: An option's registry value name is taken from its own value name, except for a list option that has a value prefix attribute: the prefix is used and the own value name only when that prefix is empty. A list option counts as prefixed whenever the attribute is present, even if empty.

rules.headline: Stored policy file value is read back…
rules.summary: A stored policy file value is read back as text for text and expandable text, a 32-bit or 64-bit number for numbers
rules.detail: A stored policy file value is read back as text for text and expandable text, a 32-bit or 64-bit number for numbers, a list of strings for multiple strings, and raw bytes for every other type.

rules.headline: When a policy lists no supported-on information
rules.summary: When a policy lists no supported-on information, it counts as supported only if the caller allows unlisted policies.
rules.detail: When a policy lists no supported-on information, it counts as supported only if the caller allows unlisted policies. The same applies to a support entry that names no known product.

rules.headline: Value in the live registry counts as present…
rules.summary: A value in the live registry counts as present when its key exists and, unless the value name is empty
rules.detail: A value in the live registry counts as present when its key exists and, unless the value name is empty, the key lists a value of that name, regardless of case. An empty name means the key itself.

rules.headline: Support entry for a product counts as met…
rules.summary: A support entry for a product counts as met in two cases.
rules.detail: A support entry for a product counts as met in two cases. The entry is not a version range and that exact product is among the chosen products. Or the product has versions beneath it, and any of those versions or their sub-products is chosen, even when the product itself is not.

rules.headline: Support entry for a product
rules.summary: A support entry for a product that has versions beneath it, whether a version range or a plain entry for a parent product
rules.detail: A support entry for a product that has versions beneath it, whether a version range or a plain entry for a parent product that is not itself chosen, counts as met when any version in its range, or a sub-product directly beneath one, is chosen. The range runs from the entry's minimum (0 if none) to its maximum (the highest version if none). A range entry never matches on its own product, and a product with no versions beneath it never matches this way.

rules.headline: Reading a value from the live registry gives…
rules.summary: Reading a value from the live registry gives nothing when the key is missing.
rules.detail: Reading a value from the live registry gives nothing when the key is missing. Signed numbers are returned as the unsigned numbers policies use, and environment variables in text are not expanded.

rules.headline: Support definition met a second time anywhere…
rules.summary: A support definition met a second time anywhere in one evaluation counts as not met, because the list of definitions seen is never emptied.
rules.detail: A support definition met a second time anywhere in one evaluation counts as not met, because the list of definitions seen is never emptied. Two entries that point at the same definition, with no cycle, make the second one not met.

rules.headline: When the caller asks for 'any' matching
rules.summary: When the caller asks for 'any' matching, a support definition whose logic is all-of needs every entry met
rules.detail: When the caller asks for 'any' matching, a support definition whose logic is all-of needs every entry met, and any other definition needs one entry met. When the caller does not ask for 'any', every definition, all-of included, is met by one entry. A definition with no entries, or none met, is met only when all are required. Plain product entries are checked before nested definitions.

rules.headline: Live registry never reports a value as marked…
rules.detail: The live registry never reports a value as marked for deletion.

rules.headline: Registry key counts as a policy key…
rules.summary: A registry key counts as a policy key when it is one of the three policy branches (software\policies, software\microsoft\windows\currentversion\policies, system\currentcontrolset\policies) or lies below one
rules.detail: A registry key counts as a policy key when it is one of the three policy branches (software\policies, software\microsoft\windows\currentversion\policies, system\currentcontrolset\policies) or lies below one, regardless of case.

actions.detail: Enables the folder box and Browse button only when the custom folder choice is selected.

actions.headline: Looks for the domain's SYSVOL policy definitions folder…
actions.detail: Looks for the domain's SYSVOL policy definitions folder and enables that choice only if it exists.

actions.detail: Opens the details window of the ADMX file double-clicked in the list.

actions.detail: Opens the selected ADMX file's details when Enter is pressed.

actions.detail: Lists the major versions of the selected top-level product.

actions.detail: Resizes the Name column so it fills the list beside the version columns.

actions.detail: Opens the product details, or shows the referenced support definition in this window.

actions.detail: Lists the minor versions of the selected major version.

actions.detail: Lets the person pick a folder in a folder dialog and puts it in the folder box.

actions.detail: Shows the details of the product's parent product in this same window.

actions.detail: Closes the window as cancelled when Escape is pressed.

actions.detail: Opens the details window of the product double-clicked.

actions.headline: Opens the selected product's details when Enter…
actions.detail: Opens the selected product's details when Enter is pressed.

actions.detail: Copies the selected node text to the clipboard on Ctrl+C.

actions.detail: Resizes the policy name column to fill the list.

actions.detail: Switches whether categories with no visible policies are shown.

actions.detail: Switches the view between user, computer and both policy sections.

actions.detail: Lists the ADMX files loaded in the workspace.

actions.detail: Lists every support definition in the workspace.

actions.detail: Shows only the menu items that apply to a category or a policy.

concerns.name: Reading and writing policy files
concerns.verdict: Business logic shared with other capabilities
concerns.purpose: Every place that changes or reads policies leans on the policy file code: loading, saving, listing values and forgetting a value.

concerns.name: Text in the chosen language
concerns.purpose: Turns a policy template's text codes into readable names and explanations, used wherever categories, products, support rules and policies are shown.

assumptions.statement: When the person's language has no exact language folder, the folder picked among those of the same primary language is the first one the operating system lists; which that is, is not stated in code.
assumptions.why: The folder listing order is left to the file system, and the template folders present are out of scope.
assumptions.ifWrong: A person could see a different regional variant of the policy text than expected when several variants are installed.

risks.headline: A failed load of policy templates leaves the workspace inconsistent.
risks.summary: Staged items survive and make later loads fail, partly filled lists make retries fail on duplicate names, and a download reloads after clearing the workspace
risks.detail: A failed load of policy templates leaves the workspace inconsistent. Staged items survive and make later loads fail, partly filled lists make retries fail on duplicate names, and a download reloads after clearing the workspace, so a failure leaves it empty. Several actions reset it; others do not.
risks.category: Data can end up wrong, lost or inconsistent

risks.headline: Comment loading and saving failures are hidden.
risks.summary: An unreadable comment file silently disables comments for that source, a failed save is dropped so typed comments are lost
risks.detail: Comment loading and saving failures are hidden. An unreadable comment file silently disables comments for that source, a failed save is dropped so typed comments are lost, and turning on the comment filter then fails with an unhandled error.
risks.category: Failures are hidden, lost or not retried

risks.headline: Importing a REG file applies it key by key to the live policy source with no rollback, and a REG source cannot read or forget values.
risks.summary: A failure leaves earlier changes in place and the person sees only a general failure message.
risks.detail: Importing a REG file applies it key by key to the live policy source with no rollback, and a REG source cannot read or forget values. A failure leaves earlier changes in place and the person sees only a general failure message.
risks.category: Data can end up wrong, lost or inconsistent

risks.headline: Policy template and comment XML files are read with default settings and no stated limit on external references.
risks.summary: The folders or domain share they come from may be writable by others, and whether external entities resolve depends on the framework default.
risks.detail: Policy template and comment XML files are read with default settings and no stated limit on external references. The folders or domain share they come from may be writable by others, and whether external entities resolve depends on the framework default.
risks.category: Input from outside is used without checks, so it can change what the code does

risks.headline: Template and comment XML files, read from a chosen folder or the domain share, are loaded with default settings and no stated limit on external references.
risks.summary: Whether those resolve rests on the framework default, which the code does not settle.
risks.detail: Template and comment XML files, read from a chosen folder or the domain share, are loaded with default settings and no stated limit on external references. Whether those resolve rests on the framework default, which the code does not settle. If they do, a crafted file on a writable share could read local files.
risks.category: Input from outside is used without checks, so it can change what the code does

risks.headline: Text typed by the person, a user identifier or a language code, is used unchecked as part of a folder path.
risks.summary: Path characters redirect where policy and version files are created or which folder is searched for definition text, using the person's own rights.
risks.detail: Text typed by the person, a user identifier or a language code, is used unchecked as part of a folder path. Path characters redirect where policy and version files are created or which folder is searched for definition text, using the person's own rights.
risks.category: Input from outside is used without checks, so it can change what the code does

risks.headline: Each template states the minimum text-file revision it needs and each text file states its own, but nothing compares them.
risks.summary: A template can be paired with text too old for it.
risks.detail: Each template states the minimum text-file revision it needs and each text file states its own, but nothing compares them. A template can be paired with text too old for it.
risks.category: Data can end up wrong, lost or inconsistent

risks.headline: If the program cannot create its settings key it carries on silently, so sources, folder, language and prompts revert each run.
risks.summary: Remembered-source values are also written one by one, so a failure can leave a mismatched pair.
risks.detail: If the program cannot create its settings key it carries on silently, so sources, folder, language and prompts revert each run. Remembered-source values are also written one by one, so a failure can leave a mismatched pair.
risks.category: Failures are hidden, lost or not retried

risks.headline: Several windows raise an unhandled error on ordinary input: double-clicking with no row selected, right-clicking with no category, an unnamed list entry, an unreadable import file, a malformed search wildcard, a removed product in a filter, or an inspector item with no match.
risks.summary: No program-wide handler is set, so the framework's default error dialog appears.
risks.detail: Several windows raise an unhandled error on ordinary input: double-clicking with no row selected, right-clicking with no category, an unnamed list entry, an unreadable import file, a malformed search wildcard, a removed product in a filter, or an inspector item with no match. No program-wide handler is set, so the framework's default error dialog appears.
risks.category: Failures are hidden, lost or not retried
